methods.name: Apply
methods.description: Create or update a session.

methods.name: Create
methods.description: Create a session.

methods.name: Update
methods.description:
Update a session: the fields update_mask names change, every other
 field keeps its stored value.

 resource.metadata.id names the session; apply finds one by slug. The slug
 changes only through rename, and a mask naming a field another door
 owns, or a path the session does not have, is refused with
 INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the path.

 An update is refused with ABORTED carrying a google.rpc.ErrorInfo detail
 (domain "stigmer.ai"):

   - ETAG_MISMATCH — resource.metadata.etag is set and the session changed
     since that etag was read: read it again and make the change again.
     No metadata.
   - WRITE_CONFLICT — the session kept changing while the update was
     being saved: try again. No metadata.

methods.name: UpdateSubject
methods.description:
Set the session subject.

 This is a targeted update that modifies only the subject field,
 leaving other session fields untouched. Use this instead of the full
 update RPC when you only need to change the session subject.

methods.name: ReviewFileChanges
methods.description:
Keep or undo the file changes a turn made, or one of its files.

 In a conversation with file review on (SessionSpec.file_review), each
 turn's file edits are applied as the agent makes them and listed in a
 stigmer.file_review.changes event. They can be decided until the
 conversation's next message is sent; then whatever is undecided is
 kept. Keep records the choice. Undo puts the file back as it was
 before the turn: at once when the turn has ended (the reply names the
 turn that does it), else when the turn's next step starts. The
 decision is appended as a stigmer.file_review.decided event.

 ## Error Conditions

 - NOT_FOUND: the change set is not one of this conversation's
 - FAILED_PRECONDITION: the conversation has moved on (a later message
   was sent), the change was already decided the other way (a decision
   is final), the file is not in the change set, or a keep of a change
   that cannot be shown whole without acknowledge_unreviewable
 - INVALID_ARGUMENT: expected_digest does not match the change

 ## Idempotency

 The same decision sent again records nothing new and starts no second
 turn.

methods.name: ConfirmToolUse
methods.description:
Allow or deny a tool use that waits for an answer.

 A call that needs a person's answer is an agent.tool_use (or
 agent.mcp_tool_use) with evaluated_permission ask, and the session goes
 idle with stop_reason requires_action naming it. The answer is appended
 as a user.tool_confirmation. A deny may carry a message, which the
 agent reads. When every waiting call of the turn is answered, the turn
 resumes; until then the session re-states requires_action with the
 calls still waiting.

 ## Error Conditions

 - NOT_FOUND: the tool use is not one of this conversation's calls that
   asked
 - FAILED_PRECONDITION: the call no longer waits (its turn moved on or
   was stopped), or it was already answered the other way (an answer is
   final)

 ## Idempotency

 The same answer sent again records nothing new and returns the event
 first recorded.

methods.name: GrantPermission
methods.description:
Allow a tool use, and every call of its class for the rest of the turn.

 The class is the call's built-in category (write, delete or shell), its
 MCP server, or, when a hook asked, that hook on that tool. The grant is
 appended as a stigmer.permission.grant after the call's
 user.tool_confirmation, and every other call of the class waiting in
 the same turn is allowed with it. A call with no class (one the
 default never asks about) is allowed alone, with no grant.

 ## Error Conditions

 As confirmToolUse.

 ## Idempotency

 The same grant sent again records nothing new.

methods.name: StopBackgroundCommand
methods.description:
Stop one command the agent runs in the background.

 A command started in the background has a
 stigmer.background_command.status with phase running, keyed to the
 agent.tool_use that started it. The request is appended as a
 stigmer.background_command.stop_requested; the turn's runner reads it
 within seconds and stops that command alone, whose status then ends
 with stopped_by person. The agent is told a person stopped it and
 carries on. The turn itself is not stopped (interrupt stops it).

 ## Error Conditions

 - NOT_FOUND: the tool use is not one of this conversation's calls that
   started a command in the background
 - FAILED_PRECONDITION: the command already ended, or its turn is not
   working

 ## Idempotency

 A second request for the same command records nothing new and returns
 the event first recorded.

methods.name: Interrupt
methods.description:
Stop the session's unfinished work.

 Appends a user.interrupt and stops every unfinished turn of the
 conversation: pending, working, waiting for an answer or paused. Each
 ends cancelled and the session goes idle with end_turn. The messages
 still queued for a turn (RunCommandController.sendMessage) are dropped
 first: they stay listed with no processed_at, never read. Files undone
 in a turn that waited are put back at once.

 ## Error Conditions

 - INVALID_ARGUMENT: session_thread_id is set (one thread alone cannot
   be stopped)
 - FAILED_PRECONDITION: the execution engine is not connected

 ## Idempotency

 An interrupt with nothing unfinished records the event and stops
 nothing.

methods.name: Delete
methods.description:
Delete a session.

 Deletion cascades to the session's runs. Billing usage
 records are immutable and unaffected — they carry their own copies of
 the session and run identifiers.

 Fails with FAILED_PRECONDITION while any run in the
 session is still active (pending, in progress, waiting for approval,
 or paused); interrupt the session or wait for it to finish first.

methods.name: AppendEvents
methods.description:
Append a run's events to its session's log.

 Only the runner acting for the run may call it, while the run is not
 finished. It accepts the events a runner produces: agent.*,
 session.thread_* and session.error. The batch is appended whole or not
 at all.

methods.name: ClaimInput
methods.description:
Take the messages queued in a run's session for the run to read.

 Only the runner acting for the run may call it, while the run works
 (pending or in progress). Every message still queued moves to the head
 of the log as this run's, with its processed_at, and is answered in
 the order sent; none when nothing waits.

methods.name: BindHarnessState
methods.description:
Record the harness's conversation id for a run's session.

 Only the runner acting for the run may call it, while the run is not
 finished. The id replaced, if any, joins the session's
 harness_state_id_history.

methods.name: Get
methods.description: Get a single session by ID.

methods.name: List
methods.description:
List all sessions with pagination and optional filtering.

 An eval run's tries are left out: each runs in a session of its own,
 read through the eval run (EvalRunQueryController.get) instead.

methods.name: ListByAgent
methods.description:
List the conversations on one agent, whichever version each runs.

 Results are filtered to the sessions the caller can view. An eval
 run's tries are left out, as in list.

methods.name: ListByChannel
methods.description:
List the conversations a channel served.

 Returns the sessions the given channel's visitors or its Slack or
 WhatsApp runtime started, newest first. The caller must be able to view
 the channel; results are additionally filtered to sessions the caller
 can view.

methods.name: ListEvents
methods.description:
List a session's events, oldest first unless desc is asked for.

 The events are Claude Managed Agents session events, in the order they
 were appended; a page holds at most page_size of them.

methods.name: StreamEvents
methods.description:
Stream a session's events as they are appended.

 Without after_seq the stream starts at the moment it opens, as Managed
 Agents' does. With after_seq it first sends the stored events after
 that seq, then the new ones, with none missing: a client that listed
 up to some seq, or whose stream ended, resumes from the last seq it
 has. A watcher that reads slowly lags behind the log and is never
 ended for it; a server that is restarting ends its streams with
 UNAVAILABLE, and a client resumes the same way.

methods.name: StreamAttention
methods.description:
Stream what needs the caller: one Attention each time a conversation
 they created in the organization stops working, because its turn
 finished, failed, or waits for their answer. A stop the caller made
 themselves (an interrupt, a terminate) sends nothing.

 It reads the conversations' log, so nothing is missed across a
 reconnect: with after_cursor the stream first sends every attention
 after that cursor, then the new ones; without, only those that come
 after it opens. A cursor is read again from a short way back, so an
 attention may come twice: a client keeps the ids it showed. A cursor
 older than a day resumes from a day ago.
 A server that is restarting ends its streams with UNAVAILABLE, and a
 client resumes with its last cursor.

methodTypes.name: UpdateSessionInput
methodTypes.description:
The changes an update makes to a session: the fields update_mask names,
 taken from resource.

fields.name: Resource
fields.description:
The session carrying the new values, named by metadata.id. Only the fields
 update_mask names are read, so the others may be left empty; the result
 is validated as a whole.

fields.name: UpdateMask
fields.description:
The paths the update changes, as proto field names (spec.instructions,
 metadata.labels). A list or map at a named path is replaced whole; "*"
 names every path an update may change.

methodTypes.name: UpdateSessionSubjectRequest
methodTypes.description: UpdateSessionSubjectRequest sets the conversation title for a session.

fields.name: Id
fields.description: Session ID to update.

fields.name: Subject
fields.description: New subject value. Empty string clears the subject.

methodTypes.name: ReviewFileChangesInput
methodTypes.description:
ReviewFileChangesInput keeps or undoes a turn's file changes, or one of
 its files.

fields.name: SessionId
fields.description: The conversation.

fields.name: ChangeSetId
fields.description: The change set, as its stigmer.file_review.changes event names it.

fields.name: Scope
fields.description: change_set (every file of the set) or file (the one file_change_id).

fields.name: FileChangeId
fields.description: The file to decide, when scope is file.

fields.name: Action
fields.description: keep or undo.

fields.name: ExpectedDigest
fields.description:
The digest of what the person saw: the file's digest for scope file,
 the set's aggregate_digest for scope change_set. A decision against a
 change that differs is refused.

fields.name: Reason
fields.description: An optional reason, kept with the decision.

fields.name: AcknowledgeUnreviewable
fields.description:
Set on a keep to keep a binary change consciously: its bytes can be
 put back, but it has no text diff to show. Ignored on an undo, and
 never relaxes expected_digest.

methodTypes.name: ReviewFileChangesResponse
methodTypes.description: ReviewFileChangesResponse answers a recorded decision.

fields.name: ReconcileRunId
fields.description:
The turn started to put undone files back now, when the decision was
 an undo on a turn that had ended; empty otherwise, or when no turn
 could be started then (the next turn puts them back before its agent
 runs).

methodTypes.name: ConfirmToolUseInput
methodTypes.description:
ConfirmToolUseInput allows or denies a tool use that waits for an answer:
 Managed Agents' user.tool_confirmation parameters, with the session.

fields.name: SessionId
fields.description: The conversation.

fields.name: ToolUseId
fields.description:
The agent.tool_use or agent.mcp_tool_use event to answer, as the
 requires_action idle's event_ids name it.

fields.name: Result
fields.description: allow or deny.

fields.name: DenyMessage
fields.description: Why the call is denied, for the agent to read; only with deny.

methodTypes.name: SessionEvent
methodTypes.description:
SessionEvent is one entry in a session's ordered event log.

 The event itself is a Claude Managed Agents session event, named and
 shaped as Anthropic's SDK types it (see the session docs for the pinned
 version). The envelope adds where the event sits: its place in the log,
 the turn (run) it belongs to and the thread that produced it.

fields.name: Seq
fields.description:
The event's place in the session's log, assigned when it is appended:
 later events have higher numbers. A queued user.message moves to the
 head of the log when a turn takes it, under a new number, so it is
 listed once, where the agent read it, and streams a second time.

fields.name: SessionId
fields.description: The session the event belongs to.

fields.name: RunId
fields.description: The run (turn) the event belongs to; empty for none.

fields.name: ThreadId
fields.description:
The thread that produced the event; empty for the session's primary
 thread.

fields.name: UserMessage
fields.description: The user sent a message.

fields.name: SessionStatusRunning
fields.description: The session started working.

fields.name: SessionStatusIdle
fields.description: The session stopped working and waits for input.

fields.name: SessionError
fields.description: An error happened.

fields.name: AgentMessage
fields.description: The agent wrote a message.

fields.name: AgentThinking
fields.description: The agent is thinking.

fields.name: AgentToolUse
fields.description: The agent called a built-in tool.

fields.name: AgentToolResult
fields.description: A built-in tool returned.

fields.name: AgentMcpToolUse
fields.description: The agent called an MCP server's tool.

fields.name: AgentMcpToolResult
fields.description: An MCP server's tool returned.

fields.name: SessionThreadCreated
fields.description: A thread (a subagent) was created.

fields.name: SessionThreadStatusRunning
fields.description: A thread started working.

fields.name: SessionThreadStatusIdle
fields.description: A thread stopped working.

fields.name: AgentThreadMessageSent
fields.description: The agent sent a message to another thread.

fields.name: AgentThreadMessageReceived
fields.description: The agent received a message from another thread.

fields.name: AgentThreadContextCompacted
fields.description: A thread's context was compacted.

fields.name: UserToolConfirmation
fields.description: A person allowed or denied a tool use that waited for an answer.

fields.name: UserInterrupt
fields.description: A person stopped the session's unfinished work.

fields.name: StigmerAgentThinking
fields.description: The text of the agent's thinking.

fields.name: StigmerPermissionAsked
fields.description: Why a tool use waits for a person's answer.

fields.name: StigmerHarnessNote
fields.description: A line the platform added to the conversation in its own voice.

fields.name: StigmerAgentStructuredOutput
fields.description: The structured output the turn produced.

fields.name: StigmerMemoryRecalled
fields.description: Which of the agent's memories the turn recalled.

fields.name: StigmerFileReviewChanges
fields.description:
The files a turn changed, offered for review (the session asked for
 file review).

fields.name: StigmerFileReviewDecided
fields.description: A turn's file changes, or one of its files, were kept or undone.

fields.name: StigmerFileReviewReconciled

fields.name: StigmerPermissionGrant
fields.description: A person allowed every call of one class for the rest of the turn.

fields.name: StigmerRunStatus
fields.description:
A turn (run) changed phase: it started, waits, paused, or ended and
 how.

fields.name: StigmerToolResultFullOutput
fields.description:
Where the whole output of a tool result that was too large to keep
 inline is stored.

fields.name: StigmerBackgroundCommandStatus
fields.description:
A command the agent started in the background began running, or
 ended and how.

fields.name: StigmerBackgroundCommandStopRequested
fields.description: A person asked to stop a command running in the background.

GrantPermissionInput allows a tool use and every call of its class for

The stigmer.permission.grant; absent when the call has no class and

fields.name: SessionId

InterruptSessionInput stops a session's unfinished work: Managed Agents'
 user.interrupt parameters, with the session.

fields.name: SessionId

fields.name: SessionThreadId

methodTypes.name: InterruptSessionResponse

fields.name: Event

fields.name: StoppedRunIds

methodTypes.name: AppendSessionEventsInput
methodTypes.description: AppendSessionEventsInput appends a run's events to its session's log.

fields.name: RunId
fields.description: The run the events belong to.

fields.name: Events
fields.description:
The events, in order. Each carries its own id, unique in the session
 (ids starting with sevt_ are the server's), and its thread; the server
 assigns seq and processed_at. A resent id with the same event is
 accepted again without a second entry.

fields.name: Previews
fields.description: Live previews to stream to the session's watchers, never stored.

methodTypes.name: AppendSessionEventsResponse
methodTypes.description:
AppendSessionEventsResponse says where each event of the request sits in
 the log.

fields.name: Events
fields.description:
One entry per event of the request, in order, by identity only: the
 envelope with its seq, and the event's type, id and processed_at. The
 content is not echoed; a resent event answers its first place.

methodTypes.name: ClaimSessionInputInput
methodTypes.description:
ClaimSessionInputInput names the run that takes its session's queued
 messages.

fields.name: RunId
fields.description: The run that reads them.

methodTypes.name: ClaimSessionInputResponse
methodTypes.description: ClaimSessionInputResponse answers the messages the run took.

fields.name: Events
fields.description:
Their user.message events as the log now holds them, in the order
 they were sent.

BindHarnessStateInput names a run and the harness's conversation id its
 session continues from.

fields.name: RunId
fields.description: The run whose session the id belongs to.

fields.name: HarnessStateId
fields.description: The harness's own conversation id.

methodTypes.name: BindHarnessStateResponse
methodTypes.description:
BindHarnessStateResponse answers the session's harness state after the
 write.

fields.name: HarnessStateId
fields.description: The id now recorded.

fields.name: HarnessStateIdHistory
fields.description: The ids the session owned before, oldest first.

methodTypes.name: ListSessionsRequest
methodTypes.description: ListSessionsRequest specifies parameters for listing sessions.

fields.name: PageSize
fields.description:
The most entries to return: 0 asks for the default page of 50, and a
 size above 100 is read as 100.

fields.name: PageToken
fields.description:
The previous response's next_page_token, to continue that list; every
 other field must equal that request's, or the call is refused.

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Organization slug to scope the results to.

 When set, only sessions of that organization are returned — the
 org-context view a console needs. When empty, results are bounded only
 by the caller's view permissions, which for a member of several
 organizations spans all of them.

fields.name: Labels
fields.description:
Only resources carrying every label given, each matched exactly (AND).
 A selective filter may answer short pages, even empty ones, that still
 carry a token.

methodTypes.name: SessionList
methodTypes.description: SessionList contains one page of sessions, newest first.

fields.name: Entries
fields.description: Sessions in this page, newest first.

fields.name: NextPageToken
fields.description:
Set when more entries may follow: pass it as page_token to continue.
 A page may be short, even empty, and still carry a token.

ID of the agent whose conversations to list: the sessions whose

fields.name: PageSize

The most entries to return: 0 asks for the default page of 50, and a
 size above 100 is read as 100.

fields.name: PageToken

The previous response's next_page_token, to continue that list; every
 other field must equal that request's, or the call is refused.

fields.name: Labels
fields.description:
Only resources carrying every label given, each matched exactly (AND).
 A selective filter may answer short pages, even empty ones, that still
 carry a token.

fields.name: PageSize

fields.name: PageToken

The previous response's next_page_token, to continue that list; every

fields.name: Labels
fields.description:
Only resources carrying every label given, each matched exactly (AND).

methodTypes.name: ListSessionEventsRequest
methodTypes.description: ListSessionEventsRequest pages through one session's event log.

fields.name: SessionId
fields.description: The session whose events to list.

fields.name: PageSize
fields.description: The most events to return, at most 1000; zero returns 100.

fields.name: PageToken
fields.description:
The previous response's next_page_token, to continue that list; every
 other field must equal that request's, or the call is refused.

fields.name: Order
fields.description: The order: asc (oldest first, the default) or desc.

fields.name: Types
fields.description:
Only events of these types, for example session.status_idle; empty
 lists every type.

fields.name: CreatedAtGt
fields.description: Only events appended after this RFC 3339 instant.

fields.name: CreatedAtGte
fields.description: Only events appended at or after this RFC 3339 instant.

fields.name: CreatedAtLt
fields.description: Only events appended before this RFC 3339 instant.

fields.name: CreatedAtLte
fields.description: Only events appended at or before this RFC 3339 instant.

fields.name: RunId
fields.description: Only the events of this run (turn); empty lists every run's.

methodTypes.name: SessionEventList
methodTypes.description: SessionEventList is one page of a session's events.

fields.name: Events

fields.name: NextPageToken

Set when more events may follow: pass it as page_token to continue.

methodTypes.name: StreamSessionEventsRequest
methodTypes.description: StreamSessionEventsRequest opens a live stream of one session's events.

fields.name: SessionId
fields.description: The session whose events to stream.

fields.name: EventDeltas
fields.description:
The event types to preview while they are produced: agent.message,
 agent.thinking, and Stigmer's stigmer.tool_output_delta (a running
 tool's output) and stigmer.run.liveness (what a working turn has open).
 Empty streams no previews.

fields.name: AfterSeq
fields.description:
Where to resume: the seq of the last event the client already has. Set,
 the stream first sends every stored event after it, in order, then the
 events appended from then on, with none missing and none repeated.
 Unset, the stream sends only the events appended after it opens.

methodTypes.name: StreamSessionEventsResponse
methodTypes.description:
StreamSessionEventsResponse is one frame of a session's event stream: a
 stored event, or a live preview of one still being produced.

fields.name: Event
fields.description: An event appended to the session's log.

fields.name: EventStart
fields.description: A preview of an event opened.

fields.name: EventDelta
fields.description: A fragment of a previewed event.

fields.name: StigmerToolOutputDelta
fields.description: A fragment of a running tool's output.

fields.name: StigmerRunLiveness
fields.description: What a working turn has open now, and for how long.

methodTypes.name: StreamAttentionRequest
methodTypes.description:
StreamAttentionRequest opens the caller's stream of what needs them in
 one organization.

fields.name: Org
fields.description: The organization whose conversations to watch.

fields.name: AfterCursor
fields.description:
Where to resume: the cursor of the last Attention the client has.
 Empty streams only what comes after the stream opens. A cursor older
 than a day resumes from a day ago.

methodTypes.name: Attention
methodTypes.description:
Attention is one conversation, created by the caller, that stopped
 working and needs them: its turn finished, failed, or waits for their
 answer.

fields.name: Id
fields.description:
The session.status_idle event it reads from: a client shows each id
 once.

fields.name: SessionId
fields.description: The conversation.

fields.name: Title
fields.description: The conversation's title (its subject), or its name when it has none.

fields.name: RunId
fields.description: The turn that stopped; empty when no turn's write ended it.

fields.name: Reason
fields.description:
Why it needs the caller: "finished" (the turn ended its work),
 "failed" (retries ran out, or a budget was reached) or "needs_answer"
 (a tool call waits for an approval).

fields.name: At
fields.description: When it stopped, RFC 3339.

fields.name: Cursor
fields.description: Where a client resumes from: StreamAttentionRequest.after_cursor.

values.description:
An installed Agent Plugins package: one thing holding skills, agents,
 hooks and MCP servers, which agents and conversations list whole.

values.name: vault
values.description:
A person's or an organization's box of logins (matched by a tool's
 address) and secrets (matched by name) that runs use.

values.name: score
values.description:
One grade of a finished run: a person's thumbs or a free run-health
 check.

values.name: scoring_rule
values.description:
AI grading switched on for one agent: its sample rate, monthly spending
 limit and judge model.

values.name: eval_run
values.description:
One run of test cases on an agent, or on a plugin on the built-in
 assistant, optionally with and without a plugin.

values.name: eval
values.description:
A set of test cases for an agent: an evals/ folder in Claude Code's
 plugin-eval format, pushed whole.

values.name: environment
values.description:
A named sandbox setup: the packages installed in every sandbox a
 conversation using it runs in, and the hosts it may reach.

values.name: file
values.description:
A file uploaded once and named by its id: given to a conversation with
 a message, held in a conversation's resources, or kept by its uploader.

values.name: plan
values.description:
Catalog entry naming a bundle of entitlements and the terms that buy it.

 Platform-level: a plan belongs to no organization, so it carries no
 authorization scope and no owner. Immutable once created; a change of
 terms is a new Plan and the old one retires.

values.name: subscription
values.description:
An organization's binding to a Plan; at most one active per organization.

 System-created: the payment system drives its lifecycle, so it has no
 owner and grants no roles. Its reads and writes authorize on the
 organization through the billing permissions.

values.name: license
values.description:
A signed grant of entitlements to a self-hosting customer for a term.

 Platform-level: issued by the cloud's operators and verified offline by
 the Enterprise server, so the customer is a value inside the license
 (which may or may not name a cloud organization) and the kind has no
 authorization scope and no owner. Claims are immutable once signed; a
 renewal is a new License.

enumTypes.name: ApiResourceVisibility
enumTypes.description:
Visibility controls who can access an API resource.
 This is orthogonal to ownership - visibility is about access control,
 while ownership (org) determines who manages the resource.

 Key distinction:
 - Ownership: Which organization controls/manages the resource
 - Visibility: Who can access/use the resource

 All resources belong to an organization. Visibility determines which
 users, inside that organization or in its child organizations, can read
 the resource. No level reaches every
 account on the server.

 The visibility levels map to FGA tuples:
 - PRIVATE: no additional viewer tuples (owner-only access)
 - ORG: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer tuple (everyone in the
   org — the org role hierarchy flows downward, so owners, admins, members
   AND read-only viewers all satisfy the organization#viewer userset)
 - CHILD_ORGS: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer
   (everyone in every child organization of the owning organization)
 - PUBLIC: retired; see the value's own comment.

values.name: visibility_private
values.description:
Only the owner, explicitly granted principals, and — for blueprint kinds
 in the cloud edition — org admins can access.
 This is the default for personal and run-scoped resources.

 Org admins count as owners of blueprint kinds (agent, channel,
 skill, plugin), so a private blueprint stays
 manageable — and visible — to its org's admins. Personal kinds
 (sessions) stay creator-only.

values.name: visibility_public
values.description:
Retired. This level made a resource readable to every account on the
 server; it is refused at create and at updateVisibility for every kind,
 and every stored row that held it has been moved to visibility_org.
 Sharing across organizations happens through plugins (a copy is
 installed and owned) or, from a parent organization to its children,
 through visibility_child_orgs.

values.name: visibility_org
values.description:
Everyone in the owning organization can access (read) this resource —
 all org roles including read-only viewers (the role just-in-time provisioning
 grants by default). Running or otherwise spending against the resource
 still requires the org-level member-or-guest permissions
 (can_create_session / can_create_run_in); org visibility widens
 read, never spend.

 FGA tuple: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer
 (The tuple once targeted organization#member, which
 excluded viewer-role users; the authorization model no longer admits
 that shape.)

values.name: visibility_child_orgs
values.description:
Everyone in every child organization of the owning organization can
 read and run this resource: the shared catalog an organization offers
 the organizations under it (spec.parent_org). Child organizations
 created later gain access automatically, and no other organization
 does. Instances, sessions, runs and vaults are never shared
 this way: each child runs the shared blueprint inside its own boundary.

 Only valid for blueprint kinds with supports_child_orgs: true, and only
 in an organization that is not itself a child.

 FGA tuple: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer

enumTypes.name: Harness
enumTypes.description:
Harness identifies the execution engine that processes agent activities
 for a session.

 Each harness corresponds to a different Temporal activity type registered
 by the runner daemon. The harness determines:
 - Which tools the agent has access to
 - How conversation state is managed (Stigmer checkpoints vs engine-native)
 - Which LLM models are available
 - Billing tier and cost structure

 HARNESS_UNSPECIFIED defaults to HARNESS_NATIVE for backward compatibility.

values.name: HARNESS_NATIVE
values.description:
Stigmer's native execution engine.

 Stigmer-managed checkpoints, custom tools, sandbox isolation,
 pause/resume, and full HITL approval flow.

values.name: HARNESS_CURSOR
values.description:
Cursor SDK execution engine.

 Cursor-managed conversation state, Cursor built-in tools + MCP,
 both local and cloud runtimes. Premium billing tier.

values.name: HARNESS_CLAUDE
values.description:
Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK execution engine.

 Approvals that stop at the exact call, conversation state mirrored to
 Stigmer. Refused until the platform offers it.

enumTypes.name: CursorMode
enumTypes.description:
CursorMode selects the Cursor SDK agent type for sessions using
 HARNESS_CURSOR.

 Determined once at session creation and never changed mid-session.
 Switching would lose Cursor-side conversation state because local
 agents (agent- prefix) and cloud agents (bc- prefix) maintain
 separate, incompatible conversation stores.

 Ignored when harness is not HARNESS_CURSOR.

values.name: CURSOR_MODE_LOCAL
values.description:
Local Cursor agent created with a local cwd configuration.

 Works with any workspace source (git or local path). Conversation
 state is carried by the Cursor SDK's native local store, which the
 runner persists on the durable workspace volume so Agent.resume()
 survives pod restart and snapshot restore.

values.name: CURSOR_MODE_CLOUD
values.description:
Cloud Cursor agent created with a cloud repos configuration.

 Requires every resource to be a git repository (HTTPS URL).
 Cursor natively manages conversation state for cloud agents.
 Feature-flagged — requires STIGMER_CURSOR_CLOUD_MODE_ENABLED.

enumTypes.name: ExecutionTarget
enumTypes.description:
ExecutionTarget specifies where session activities are executed.

 Determines whether the runner that processes agent activities lives on the
 client's machine (desktop app or CLI) or in a cloud-provisioned sandbox.
 Set at session creation time and immutable once a run has started —
 workspace state may not be portable between local and cloud environments.

values.name: EXECUTION_TARGET_LOCAL
values.description:
Client's embedded runner handles activities.

 Desktop app or CLI spawns a local runner process that polls the
 session's task queue. No server-side provisioning needed.

values.name: EXECUTION_TARGET_CLOUD
values.description:
Server provisions a cloud sandbox for execution.

 The control plane triggers EnsureSessionSandbox to create an isolated
 environment with a runner polling the session's task queue.

enumTypes.name: GitWriteBackMode
enumTypes.description: GitWriteBackMode controls the platform's git workflow for a git-backed workspace entry.

values.name: GIT_WRITE_BACK_BRANCH_AND_PR
values.description: Create a branch and pull request from the agent's file changes after the run completes.

resourceDescription: Session represents a multi-turn conversation thread with an agent.

statusType.name: SessionStatus
statusType.description: SessionStatus contains system-managed state for a session.

fields.name: Audit
fields.description: Standard audit information (created_at, updated_at, created_by, etc.)

fields.name: AgentId
fields.description:
ID of the agent spec.agent_ref resolved to when it was last written.
 Empty when the session names no agent: the built-in assistant answers.

fields.name: AgentVersionHash
fields.description:
Content hash of the agent version this conversation runs
 (AgentStatus.version_hash when the reference resolved; resolvable
 through AgentQueryController.getVersion with agent_id).

 Each turn runs this version and records it on its own status. Empty
 when agent_id is empty, or when the agent had no recorded version when
 the reference resolved; such a conversation runs the agent as it is
 when each turn starts.

fields.name: VaultAttachers
fields.description:
Who attached each of this resource's vaults, by vault id: the account
 whose permission to use the vault each run checks when it has no
 person.

fields.name: State
fields.description:
Whether the session is working: running (a turn works) or idle (it
 waits for input), the newest session.status_running or
 session.status_idle event's word. A session none of whose turns ever
 worked reads idle.

fields.name: HarnessStateId
fields.description:
Harness-specific state identifier for conversation continuity.

 Populated after the first run completes; empty until then. It is the
 harness's own conversation id:

 - NATIVE: the native harness's thread id, "thread-{session_id}".

 - CURSOR: Cursor SDK agent ID (e.g., "agent-xxx" or "bc-xxx")
   returned by Agent.create(). Used for Agent.resume() on
   subsequent runs.

fields.name: HarnessStateIdHistory
fields.description:
Prior harness state identifiers this session has owned, oldest first.

 A session can span multiple harness-side conversations: when the
 cursor-runner's resume fails, it creates a fresh Cursor agent and
 replaces harness_state_id, and the replaced id lands here.

fields.name: RoutineId
fields.description:
The routine whose fire started this conversation; empty for every other
 conversation.

fields.name: Environment
fields.description:
The Environment this conversation runs in, whichever named it; unset
 when none applies.

fields.name: EnvironmentSource
fields.description: Which choice environment came from.

statusNestedTypes.name: ApiResourceAudit
statusNestedTypes.description: ApiResourceAudit contains both spec-level and status-level audit details.

fields.name: SpecAudit
fields.description: Audit info for the resource's specification (desired state).

fields.name: StatusAudit
fields.description: Audit info for the resource's status (actual state).

statusNestedTypes.name: ApiResourceAuditActor
statusNestedTypes.description:
ApiResourceAuditActor represents the entity that performed an action.

 This is the platform's single actor vocabulary: every "who did this"
 reference (created_by / updated_by, version-history applied_by / pushed_by,
 approval resolved_by_actor) uses this message, so actor rendering is
 uniform across all surfaces.

fields.name: Id
fields.description: Unique identifier of the actor.

fields.name: Avatar
fields.description: URL to the actor's avatar image.

fields.name: DisplayName
fields.description:
Human-readable display name (e.g. "Ada Lovelace"). Empty when unknown;
 renderers fall back to email, then id.

fields.name: Email
fields.description:
Email address of the actor. Empty when unknown or not applicable
 (e.g. machine accounts).

fields.name: MintedBy
fields.description:
The service account whose key minted the user token the actor acted
 through. Empty for every other credential, and on an actor that records
 no act (an account's profile lookup).

fields.name: CreatedBy
fields.description: Actor who created this resource.

fields.name: CreatedAt
fields.description: Timestamp when the resource was created.

fields.name: UpdatedBy
fields.description: Actor who last updated this resource.

fields.name: UpdatedAt
fields.description: Timestamp when the resource was last updated.

fields.name: Event
fields.description: Type of the last event (e.g., "created", "updated").

statusNestedTypes.name: ApiResourceReference
statusNestedTypes.description:
Generic reference to any API resource.
 Used across resources to reference other resources (e.g., Vault, Agent, Skill).
 Canonical written format: "org/slug" (e.g., "acme/web-search", "acme/my-agent").

 A reference has three forms:
 - Written: by name (org and slug), by id, or by both. A write that carries
   both must have them agree, or it is refused naming both. A name is
   resolved to its resource's id when the referring resource is written.
 - Stored: org (the organization's id), kind, id and version. The slug is
   not stored, so a reference keeps pointing at the resource it meant when
   that resource is renamed, and never at a new resource that takes its old
   name after it is deleted.
 - Returned: as stored, with slug filled with the resource's current name.
   A reference whose resource was deleted is returned with an empty slug.

 The kind a reference names is the kind its field declares
 (reference_kind); a reference that carries another kind is refused.

 Every reference in a resource's spec is checked when the resource is
 written: the target must exist, and a target in another organization
 must be one the writing organization's parent shares with its child
 organizations (visibility_child_orgs) to be referenced at all. A blueprint may not be
 more visible than the skills, plugins and agents it references, so
 what a person can run they can also read. A reference that fails the
 check is refused at write, never at run.

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Organization that owns the referenced resource, by slug or id.

 When non-empty: an organization slug (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens,
 starts with a letter, 2-63 characters; e.g. "stigmer", "acme-corp") or an
 organization id (org_<ulid>). The server stores the id, so a stored
 reference keeps pointing at its organization across a rename.

 When empty: the reference is relative — the server resolves it to the parent
 resource's organization at write time. All stored and returned references
 always have org populated (absolute form, the id).

 Use empty org for same-org references (the common case).
 An explicit other org is accepted only when that organization is your
 organization's parent and shares the resource with its children
 (visibility_child_orgs).

fields.name: Kind
fields.description: Kind of the referenced resource (e.g., SKILL, AGENT, PLUGIN).

fields.name: Slug
fields.description:
Resource slug (user-friendly identifier, unique within org).
 Format: lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens, must start with a letter
 and end with a letter or digit (e.g., "web-search", "variance-reporter").
 Length: 2-63 characters.

 Written to name the resource; never stored; returned filled with the
 resource's current name, empty when the resource was deleted.

fields.name: Version
fields.description:
The version of a skill, a plugin or a subagent the reference asks for;
 every other kind ignores it.

 Formats:
 - empty or "latest": the latest version;
 - a tag (e.g. "stable", "v1.0"): the version the tag names;
 - a 64-character hash: that exact version, which never changes.

 When it is read: a skill or plugin reference is resolved at the start
 of each turn, so a reference without a hash follows each new push, and
 the run records the version it loaded (RunStatus.loaded_versions). A
 subagent reference is resolved once, when the agent that lists it is
 saved, and the saved reference carries the hash it resolved to.

fields.name: Id
fields.description:
The referenced resource's id: what a stored reference holds. Optional
 on write, where the slug may name the resource instead; an id no
 resource of the kind holds answers as a missing resource. At most 64
 characters.
